To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sharing of information and data is essential to the progress of the chemical sciences and that the chemical sciences have a responsibility to share information and data.

the sharing of data and information is important for the progress of science; that the chemical sciences have been slow to embrace this concept; and that the chemical sciences are in danger of falling behind the other disciplines in their ability to share and exchange information.

the chemical sciences have been late in recognizing the importance of sharing data, that there is a pressing need for the development of a chemical Semantic Web, and that the grand challenges for chemistry are to establish a chemical data commons and to develop a chemical data curation framework.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the chemical Semantic Web, and the application of Semantic Web technologies to the representation, management, and analysis of chemical information.
the management, curation, and exchange of chemical information, and with the development and application of the tools and technologies required to support these activities.

the development of tools, standards, and methodologies to support the sharing of chemical information, with the ultimate goal of improving the efficiency of the research process and enhancing scientific discovery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chemical sciences have much to learn from the experience of other disciplines, especially biology.
the sharing of chemical information is a matter of importance, and that the sharing and exchange of chemical information will be of even greater importance in the future.
chemical information matters, and that it matters that we do something about the sharing of that information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chemical community has a lot of catching up to do, but the rewards for doing so will be great.
the sharing of chemical data and information, and the development of tools to enable that, are essential to the advancement of science.
chemical information matters, and that the e Research perspective provides a valuable insight to the challenges and opportunities for the future of the discipline.
The main takeaway from our work is that

chemical information matters and that it is important that chemists take responsibility for the management and sharing of their data, and that the community should encourage the development of tools and standards that facilitate this.
chemical information matters, and that the chemical sciences are ready for e Science.
the chemical sciences can and must embrace open science and e Research.
